$comment: LP FIDELITY LEDGER. Each entry is a geometric quantity measured on real LilyPond,
paired with the difference Lily# currently shows. See README.md for how to add or
regenerate an entry. The 'lilypond' numbers are DATA: they change only by re-running
the probes in probes/ against lilypond.exe and pasting what it prints.
residual = lilysharp - lilypond, in staff-spaces. A non-zero residual MUST carry a
'why'. Naming the defect is the goal; where it is not yet isolated, say so with an
'OPEN:' prefix and state exactly what is unexplained. What is forbidden is a silent
baseline. Both directions of change are failures: a residual that grows is a
regression, and a residual that shrinks is progress that must be recorded on purpose
so it appears in the diff rather than being absorbed.
The count of exact entries and the total |residual| are the headline fidelity numbers.

So the cause is the same rounding that moved the other nine measured values -- it is bounded by that rounding (<= 7e-5) and it arrived on the same commit -- but WHICH glyph metric carries the 5.4e-6 through Staff_spacing's /7 has not been isolated. accidental.single-natural-to-notehead.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (-0.017672 -> 0). The single-note / grace accidental DRAW was a SECOND placement model: chords place accidentals through AccidentalColumn.CalculatePositions (position_apes, the REAL glyph right skyline) then DrawAccidentalAtInkLeft, but a single NoteItem (SharedRenderer.Noteheads.cs) and grace (GraceNotes.cs) drew via DrawAccidental at a FIXED AccidentalNoteGap 0.35. Measured on 2.26.0 (barline-spacing.ly score NAT, a c-natural in D major): HEAD anchor 11.569272 (ext 0 . 1.962), natural ACC anchor 10.535000 (ext 0 . 0.6666), so the natural's ink clears the head at 0.367672 -- NOT 0.35 -- and HEAD - ACC anchor = 1.034272. OPENED at residual -0.017672 (predicted to the digit): Lily# drew the natural at head - natWidth(0.6666) - 0.35 = head - 1.0166, so HEAD - ACC read 1.016600. THE FIX: route the single-note / grace accidental DRAW through AccidentalPlacement.CalculateSinglePosition (the real skyline, the SAME path the spacing reservation already uses -- so draw = reserve) then DrawAccidentalAtInkLeft. MEASURED after: Lily# 1.034272 (residual -0.00000007, within tolerance) EXACT. Sharps (Left 0, box) are byte-unchanged; naturals move 0.017672 LEFT onto LilyPond's position. This ALSO fixed a flat draw bug the same fix exposed -- see accidental.single-flat-to-notehead.

accidental.single-flat-to-notehead.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (+0.120000 -> 0). A SECOND defect the single-note-accidental unification exposed, NOT anticipated by the handoff (which claimed sharp/flat 'match'): the flat's ink starts 0.12 ss LEFT of its origin (LILC bbox left -0.12). The old DrawAccidental seated the glyph origin at head - accWidth - 0.35 with accWidth = the FULL width 0.92 (Right 0.8 - Left -0.12), so the flat's ink-right landed at head - 0.47 -- gap 0.47, NOT LilyPond's 0.35. OPENED at residual +0.120000 (predicted to the digit): Lily# drew the flat origin at head - 0.92 - 0.35 = head - 1.27, so HEAD - ACC read 1.270000. THE FIX is the same one that closed the natural: routing the draw through CalculateSinglePosition + DrawAccidentalAtInkLeft, which anchors on the glyph's ink-left (bbox.Left aware) rather than assuming the ink starts at the origin, so the flat lands on LilyPond's 0.35 gap. barline.next.time-change-to-notehead.why: CLOSED to +0.000000433 by porting Pango's quantisation LITERALLY, from LilyPond's own constants rather than by fitting. The difference was never a wrong glyph metric: LilyPond snaps a text width to a whole device pixel, and one device pixel is INCH_TO_BP / (PANGO_RESOLUTION * output_scale) staff spaces = 72 * 72.27 / (1200 * 5 * 25.4) = 0.034143 ss (lily/pango-font.cc:109-112 scale_, PANGO_RESOLUTION 1200 at lily/include/pango-font.hh:75, INCH_TO_BP 72 / INCH_TO_PT 72.27 at lily/include/dimensions.hh:31,27). Round the true advance 1.600000 to that grid and it lands on 46.86 -> 47 pixels = 1.604735, matching all ten digits to 1e-15. The residual 4.3e-7 is float noise in that arithmetic, not an unexplained sliver. ⚠️ SAME MECHANISM AS staff.staff.dynamic-under-whole-note's -0.000076, and that one is STILL open on purpose: a width needs only this single snap of one advance, but a skyline needs the whole OUTLINE quantised, which is a larger port. ⚠️ NOT closed by this, and recorded so it is not mistaken for closed: Lily# quantises the FATTENED digit advance, which equals the ASCII fetaText digit LilyPond actually sets ONLY for the digit 4 (both 1.600000); the fattened '1' is 1.292 where the ASCII '1' is 1.268, so a non-4 signature digit would quantise the wrong base. No ledger point measures one yet. Original account, of how the source was first located, follows. ly:time-signature::print builds a MARKUP and hands it to grob-interpret-markup (scm/time-signature.scm:18-29), and markup text is measured by the text layout engine, not by the music-font path Lily# and the rest of this corpus use. Asked both ways on one and the same grob on 2.24.4: ly:font-get-glyph 'fattened.four' gives 1.600000 while (markup #:number "4") gives 1.604735. So Lily#'s 1.600000 is not a stale or wrong constant — it is exactly what LilyPond's own music-font path reports for that glyph; the two paths simply disagree. Ruled out as the source of 1.604735, for all ten digits: the LILC bbox, the raw outline bounds, the advance, the plain digit family at U+0030-0039 as well as fattened at U+E0B4-U+E0BF, and a font-build difference (LilyPond 2.24.4 ships a different-sized emmentaler-20.otf than the repo copy, but their digit metrics are identical). The markup widths group 0/2/8 at 1.468162, 3/5/7 at 1.331589 and 6/9 at 1.365732, a grouping no metric in the font file reproduces, and a two-digit string is not the concat of two one-digit widths (off by 0.102430 either way) — both consistent with a shaped text run. Closing this needs that text pipeline's metrics, not a constant. The 1.600000 rides through Staff_spacing untouched (the space-alist ideal binds here, not the 0.3 + min_dist correction), so the residual is exactly the width difference. Was -1.454735 before the boundary column existed.

page.first-staff-refpoint.why: EXACT. LilyPond seats the first system with top-system-spacing's SPRING, and at force 0 a spring is max(min_distance, ideal_distance) (lily/spring.cc:219-237), so basic-distance 6 beats the ink floor -- ink above the refpoint (2.000000, the staff's own half height on this probe) plus padding 1 -- and the staff lands at top-margin + 6.000000 exactly. Lily# returned the floor alone and sat 3.000000 too high. Closing it took two steps IN ORDER, and the order is the finding: the placement had to move into the refpoint frame FIRST, because top-system-spacing aims at the staff's MIDDLE line while Lily# stacks systems by the top staff's TOP LINE. Porting the max() onto the unconverted anchor lands the top line on the value LilyPond puts the refpoint at -- measured 2026-07-22, that moves the residual -3.000000 -> +2.000000 rather than to 0. What this does NOT cover: the top spring's STRETCH under page justification (set_default_stretch_strength = ideal_distance, spring.cc:213-216). Lily# pins the first system and stretches only the inter-system springs; this probe is a natural-length page, so that difference cannot show here.

system.natural-distance.why: EXACT. system-system-spacing's basic-distance, 12, and the first Y quantity in this corpus to be confirmed rather than assumed: HANDOFF had it as 'a match' from an SVG reading at two decimals, which cannot tell 12.00 from 12.004. Measured through RecordingDocumentContext it is 12.000000 on both sides. Note what this does NOT cover: the probe is the LAST page of a score that fits one page, so the gap is the spring's natural length. The STRETCHED regime is now carried by system.stretched-distance.

page.stretched.first-staff-refpoint.why: Was -0.025482000 (seeded before the change, predicted exactly), closed to +0.000371455 by porting the chain. The remainder is NOT structural: it is the last-bottom spring's floor, and it is the same 0.044994 that system.stretched-distance carries -- see that entry. LilyPond builds ONE chain of springs per page -- top-system-spacing, one spring per system pair, then last-bottom-spacing -- and solves it against page_height_ = paper-height - top-margin - bottom-margin (page-layout-problem.cc:780-804, Simple_spacer). On a full page every spring in that chain carries the SAME force, so the top spring stretches too: measured on 2.26.0 the first refpoint sits at top-margin + 6.025482 rather than the natural 6.000000. The chain reproduces that to six digits from the source alone: (6 + 6f) + 12*(12 + 60f) + 4.544994 = 157.628268 gives f = 0.00424693, hence 6.025482 and 12.254816. The 4.544994 is last-bottom-spacing blocked at its own floor (padding 1 + 3.544994 of ink below the last refpoint). PREDICTION: Lily# currently pins the first system at its natural distance and stretches only the inter-system springs, so this should read 11.690551 (residual -0.025482) before the port and 11.716033 (residual 0) after.

system.stretched-distance.why: Was +0.089206333 before the chain was ported; the port took 96 percent of it. The remainder is ONE quantity, and it is not the spacing model: the ink hanging below the LAST system's refpoint reads 3.500000 in Lily# against 3.550000 in LilyPond. Everything else in the chain agrees to six digits. That 0.050000 was first mis-attributed here to half of LilyPond's staff-line thickness, from a figure (3.544994) that was arithmetic on a ROUNDED gap; reading the probe's raw per-system dump instead gives 3.550000000 exactly, on every system of both pages. The real cause is the notehead: the lowest note is c' with its head 3.000000 below the refpoint, so LilyPond's ink puts the head's half-height at 0.550000, while Lily# seeds its vertical skyline from EngravingDefaults.NoteheadHeight = 1.0, a nominal staff space. Lily# ALREADY has the true ink -- GlyphMetricsGenerated.NoteheadBlack is (-0.545000 .. 0.545000) from the LILC table -- so this is the vertical half of what ec7a2254 did for X, still not wired to the skyline. Fixing that accounts for 0.045000 of the 0.050000 and touches every vertical skyline, so it is its own island; the last 0.005000 (LilyPond 0.550000 against LILC's 0.545000) is NOT yet explained and must not be papered over. The system spring of the same chain as page.stretched.first-staff-refpoint, on the SAME page -- page 1 of book J, which is full. Uniform across all 12 gaps in LilyPond's dump. The predicted DIRECTION was right and the magnitude was not: Lily# solves its force over the inter-system springs ALONE (no top spring, no last-bottom spring in the chain), so the force comes out too large, but the guess of 'roughly 12.29' was copied from a stale HANDOFF figure rather than derived. Derived from Lily#'s own PASS 2 it is exact: it fills to the bottom margin with the last system's INK, leaving 4.128268 to share over 12 gaps at equal stretch = +0.344022 each, i.e. 12.344022. LilyPond instead gives that last spring last-bottom-spacing's floor (padding 1 + the ink) and lets it stretch (stretchability 30), and adds the top spring (inverse stretch 6) to the same chain. PREDICTION: 0 after porting the chain. Do NOT read this entry on the last page: ragged-last-bottom makes that page a fixed_force_solution of the PREVIOUS page's force, which is a different measurement (page-breaking.cc:565-575).

page.stretched.systems-on-first-page.why: MEASURED EXACT ON ARRIVAL, which is the finding: this probe does NOT catch the defect it was seeded for, and page.tight.* had to be built because of it. Everything else on this page describes how a page holding N systems is spaced; nothing has ever measured N. LilyPond prices a page against `page_height_ - min_whitespace_at_top_of_page(first) - min_whitespace_at_bottom_of_page(last)` (lily/page-spacing.cc:30-41), and those two terms are the page breaker's ONLY knowledge of the top-system and last-bottom springs. Each is `max(0, max(padding, minimum-distance -/+ translate))` (page-breaking.cc:1785-1823). On the shipping specs top-system-spacing and last-bottom-spacing both carry minimum-distance 0 and padding 1, and translate is the system's own up/down reach, so BOTH terms evaluate to exactly 1.000000 and LilyPond's usable band is 157.628268 - 2 = 155.628268. Lily#'s PageSpacing.CalcForce subtracts the MARGINS only, so it hands the breaker 157.628268 -- 2.000000 ss MORE room than LilyPond has. That is the whole of the divergence HANDOFF 2-8 records as `PageBreaker is out of sync with the chain`, expressed as a number for the first time. PREDICTION was: Lily# fits at least LilyPond's 13 and, if 2.000000 is enough for one more, 14 -- residual 0 or +1, never negative. MEASURED: 0. The prediction's bound held, and the answer is the uninteresting end of it: 2.000000 is not enough for a 14th system here. The reason turned out to be deeper than slack, and is worth keeping -- on default paper this count is not decided by capacity AT ALL. Raising the first system by up to four octaves (eight ledger steps, measured on 2.26.0) leaves LilyPond at 13 every time, so the breaker is choosing from the force each candidate page solves to, not from a rod hitting a ceiling. That is why this entry reads exact while the model behind it is wrong, and why page.tight.* had to shrink the paper before anything would bind. Keep it as the A4 control. LilyPond measured on 2.26.0: 13 on page 1, 8 on page 2.

page.stretched.page-count.why: The companion to page.stretched.systems-on-first-page: the per-page count alone cannot tell an over-filling breaker from one that simply paginates differently, because moving one system off page 1 and onto page 2 leaves the total unchanged. 21 systems at LilyPond's 13 + 8 fit two pages either way, so PREDICTION: 2, residual 0, BEFORE and AFTER the fix. An entry that is expected to stay green is worth having here precisely because it is the control -- if it ever moves, the change did something other than re-price the page, and the sibling entry alone could not tell me that.

page.tight.page-count.why: RE-MEASURED 2026-07-25 after book T was given `indent = 0`. It was the only page book in page-vertical.ly without one, so it engraved at LilyPond's DEFAULT 15mm while its Lily# twin ran at 0 (Lily# indents only for instrument names) -- the two sides were not setting the same page, and this entry's 2 was read off the indented one. Measured both ways on the same tight paper (jn-line-forces.ly, TPT and TPD): at indent 0 LilyPond takes FIVE systems of eight bars on ONE page; at the default indent SIX systems cut 6,7,7,7,7,6 over two. The six was the indent, not the page breaker and not paging. With the pair comparable LilyPond reads 1 page / 5 systems and so does Lily#, which is what this entry and page.tight.systems-on-first-page now record. ⚠️ THE OLD ZERO WAS CANCELLATION: Lily# reached six systems because the invented OverfullPenalty forbade the compressed five-system solution, and six systems then needed two pages -- an invented constant agreeing with an unintended indent. That is section 5.2's two-defects-cancelling shape. The paragraph kept below is the history that is still true of the PAGE arithmetic, which this correction does not touch. PREVIOUS TEXT: Now exact, and read together with page.tight.systems-on-first-page: at 70 staff spaces both sides take two pages and cut them 5 + 1. It was seeded at 72 where it read -1 (Lily# one page against LilyPond's two) and the three ports below closed that; the probe then moved to 70 because 72 became Lily#'s own flip point and the entry would have swung on unrelated changes. Re-measured 2026-07-22 with a one-line-per-BOOK dump after the earlier per-PAGE dump was found to be losing lines: LilyPond takes two pages for every height up to 75 and Lily# up to 76, so 70 sits five or six staff spaces inside BOTH plateaus. ⚠️ An earlier note here said LilyPond stayed at two pages through 77 and flipped at 79; that was read off truncated dumps and is WRONG. What actually happens at 76 and 77 is not a paging difference at all -- see page.tight.systems-on-first-page. History and model follow. Six systems on 72-staff-space paper: LilyPond takes two pages for every height from 69 to 77 and only reaches one at 79. Lily# reaches one page at 71 -- SEVEN staff spaces early -- so at 72 it prints one page where LilyPond prints two. Three LP-sourced divergences in the breaker, all measured: (1) constrained-breaking.cc:555 sets `inverse_hooke_ = full_height() + system_system_space_` = 7.35 + 12 = 19.35 per line, while Lily# uses `max(0.1, Stretchability/60)` = 1.0 -- a factor of 19 in the force denominator, and NOT the same formula at all (the breaker does not use stretchability). This is the /60 transcription cfdf85b4 abolished in the placement chain, still alive in the breaker. (2) page-spacing.cc:30-41 prices the page against `page_height_ - min_whitespace_at_top_of_page(first) - min_whitespace_at_bottom_of_page(last)`; each is `max(0, max(padding, minimum-distance -/+ translate))` (page-breaking.cc:1785-1823) and on the shipping specs both come to exactly 1.000000, so Lily# hands the breaker 2.000000 ss too much. (3) LilyPond's `bottom_padding_` is only ever assigned 0 (constrained-breaking.cc:621) so its term is inert, while Lily# subtracts the system's padding 1.000000 there. PREDICTION: 2 after all three are ported. If it lands on 2 with only some of them, the rest are still wrong and the entry is passing by cancellation -- page.tight.systems-on-first-page is the cross-check.

page.tight.systems-on-first-page.why: RE-READ 2026-07-25 with book T given `indent = 0` (see page.tight.page-count for why it had none and what the indent was worth). The VALUE is unchanged -- LilyPond still puts 5 systems on page 1 -- but what it means is not: at indent 0 those five are the WHOLE score on ONE page, not the first page of a 5 + 1 split. So this entry no longer says anything about where LilyPond cuts a two-page book; it says how many systems the line breaker makes, and both sides now make five of eight bars. ⚠️ The paragraph below is the account of the orphan penalty, which is still exactly right about the defect it names and is kept for that; its 5 + 1 framing belongs to the indented engraving. PREVIOUS TEXT: Closed. LilyPond puts 5 systems on page 1 and 1 on page 2 for every paper height up to 75, so the split is a property of the model and not of the exact height; Lily# cut 4 + 2 until the FOURTH divergence was found. ⚠️ ABOVE that plateau the two sides stop being comparable, and the reason is structural rather than arithmetic: at 76 and 77 LilyPond does not fit six systems onto one page, it RE-BREAKS the music into FIVE systems and puts those on one page (measured on a single-book probe: one SVG, 25 staff lines). LILYPOND-REF: lily/optimal-page-breaking.cc:139-173 -- Optimal_page_breaking::solve sweeps sys_count DOWNWARD from the line breaker's ideal, runs the full page spacing for every line-division configuration at each count, and keeps the global argmin of demerits; the page result therefore CHOOSES the line breaking. Lily# breaks lines once and pages afterwards, so that answer is unreachable for it at any spacing accuracy. Lily#'s own six-on-one-page threshold is 77 against LilyPond's 78 -- one staff space -- but do not read that as 'nearly right': the 76-77 window is a different shape of output, not a rounding. Keep this entry at 70 where both sides are in the same regime. It was not in the rod, and not in any of the three formulas ported before it: it was the ORPHAN PENALTY, charged on a condition LilyPond does not have. LilyPond spends orphan_penalty() only when lines_[page_start].last_markup_line_ or lines_[page_start-1].first_markup_line_ is set (page-spacing.cc:375-383) -- a multi-line markup PARAGRAPH split across a page boundary. Those flags come from a markup line's Prob (constrained-breaking.cc:633-636) and a music system's Line_details leaves both false with nothing ever setting them (constrained-breaking.hh:115-116), so music can never trigger it. Lily# was charging it for 'a lone system on the last page', which is exactly the shape of LilyPond's own 5 + 1, at 100000 against force-squared demerits of about 0.001 -- so that one invented condition decided every page break by itself. The old code cited page-breaking.cc:269 for it, which is where the VALUE is read from paper, not where it is applied: a LILYPOND-REF beside a formula is not evidence that the formula matches it (HANDOFF 5.2.1 (1)). Read with page.tight.page-count, which stayed exact throughout: the pair now agrees with LilyPond on both the number of pages and where the cut falls.

page.clef.first-staff-refpoint.why: Was +0.012727149; the clef is now seeded into the vertical skylines and it closes to -0.000082769. The seeded prediction was exact to the digit, and closing it needed a SECOND defect fixed: LayoutEngine's single-page path added SystemSpacing * 0.5 = 4 as the inter-system padding where LilyPond's system-system-spacing uses 1, so the clef's ink bound a spring LilyPond leaves at basic-distance. The remaining -8e-05 is the same LILC-vs-skyline sliver as system.clef-bounded-distance carries; see there. Original entry follows. Book S is book J's music moved inside the staff (b' on the middle line, up-stem stopping 3.5 above it) so that NOTHING hangs below the middle line and the deepest ink on every system is the CLEF. LilyPond's clef is an ordinary inside-staff grob and joins the staff's vertical skyline, reaching 3.540 below the refpoint, so it sets last-bottom-spacing's floor and through it the page's force. Lily#'s SkylineBuilder never seeds a clef at all -- it seeds the staff lines, notes, rests, accidentals, ledgers, dynamics and articulations -- so its deepest ink here should be the staff's own bottom line, 2.000000. PREDICTION, from Lily#'s own chain with the last spring blocked at padding 1 + 2.000000 = 3.000000: f = 4.628268/726 = 0.00637500, hence a first refpoint of 11.728801 (residual +0.012727) and a gap of 12.382500. Book W cannot catch this: its lowest notehead reaches 3.545, five thousandths PAST the clef, so W reads correct even with no clef in the skyline. Confirmed by measuring book S twice on 2.26.0, once with these notes and once with rests down to a 128th (glyph bottom 3.05 below the middle line): both give the identical 11.716074 and 12.255229, which is only possible if a third grob is setting them.

staff.staff.upper-note-to-lower-lines.why: EXACT. Was -0.050000, closed by seeding the staff lines as INK, and the prediction was exact both times -- seeded at -0.050000 before the change and landing on 0. THE STAFF SYMBOL'S EXTENT: Lily# seeded the staff lines at their CENTRE (+/-2.0, SkylineBuilder.SeedStaffSymbol) where LilyPond's skyline carries their INK (+/-2.05, half of the 0.1 line thickness past the centre). Asked of the grob itself, probes/glyph-skyline.ly reports StaffSymbol ext AND vertical-skylines both as (-2.05 . 2.05), so this is not an inference. SEEDED BEFORE THE CHANGE (HANDOFF 5.3) and the prediction was exact: -0.050000 measured against -0.050000 predicted. note-to-note.quarter-shortest.why: EXACT, and the PAIR against note-to-note.quarter: the same quarter-to-quarter gap, 3.002245 here against 3.704200 there, differing only in what the score's OTHER notes are. Spacing_spanner::find_shortest does not use the shortest note in the score; it takes the most common per-measure shortest and averages it with base-shortest-duration (1/8). NN's most common shortest IS 1/8, so its average is 1/8 again and the averaging is INVISIBLE there -- which means every duration-space point in this corpus was measured in the one regime where that step does nothing. Here the most common shortest is 1/4, global_shortest is 3/16, and a quarter's ratio is 4/3: (2 + log2 4/3) * 1.2 - 1.2 + 1.304200 = 3.002245. Lily# reproduces it to nine digits, so its port of the averaging is right and not merely untested. Section 5.2.1 item 4: exact is not the same as correct, but exact in a regime the corpus never entered is new information.

How many notes the LINE BREAKER puts on the first system of a justified score: LilyPond 5 bars (30 heads), Lily# 4 (24). justified.note-to-note.quarter.why: SEEDED 2026-07-25, the moment justified.first-system.heads went exact and the two engravers finally put the same five bars on this system. The quarter gap on a JUSTIFIED line, read from the same JN dump that gives the head count: `bar= 1 n=30 first= 8.585000 quarter 3.765697 eighth 2.534949`. Its ragged twin note-to-note.quarter is exact at 3.704200, so this point sees only what justification adds. It cannot. LilyPond's own note_spacing sets `inverse_stretch_strength = fraction * max (0.1, len - min)` with min = the spacing INCREMENT, not the skyline minimum (lily/spacing-basic.cc; SpacingRules.CreateSpring carries the same REF), so a stretched line never consults the skyline minimum at all and MinItemGap is invisible in this regime. The knob binds only where a spring is compressed ONTO its minimum, so the key that removal needs is a COMPRESSED note-to-note point, which this corpus still does not have. What this pair does pin is that justification itself is exact once both sides break alike.

justified.note-to-note.eighth.why: The eighth gap of the same justified line, from the same dump, and the pair with justified.note-to-note.quarter: both springs stretch on ONE solved force, so their residuals must move together. The eighth is the more sensitive of the two — its ideal is smaller, so any error in a spring's stretchability is a larger share of it — which is why both were recorded rather than one, and why their agreeing at 1e-7 is what says the stretch model is right rather than cancelling. See justified.note-to-note.quarter for the prediction this pair REFUTED (that it would be the key for GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4: a stretched line never consults the skyline minimum, so that knob is invisible here and its key must be a COMPRESSED point).

compressed.note-to-note.quarter.why: CLOSED the day it opened, by the port it was opened for: GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 is gone from the note-to-note path and the gap is built the way LilyPond builds it -- each grob's extra-spacing-width folded into its own spacing box (separation-item.cc:166-179), the spring minimum taken as the padding-free skyline distance with skyline-vertical-padding 0.08 (note-spacing.cc:78-83), and the ROD as that distance plus the spacing spanner's padding 0.1 (spacing-spanner.cc:315-316 into separation-item.cc:56). Lily# now reads 1.604200000 against LilyPond's 1.604200. The invented knob was 0.4 of gap on 1.304200 of ink; the port is 0.1 + (0.1 + 1.304200 + 0.1), which is the same number reached from LilyPond's own two steps instead of one made-up one. HISTORY, kept because it is how the point came to be right: The note-to-note gap of a line squeezed until the ROD binds, which is the only regime in which that floor is observable. ⚠️ FIRST MEASURED WRONG, and the correction is the point: with middle C as the pitch LilyPond read 1.956300, and that is not the head-to-head minimum at all -- c' in a treble staff carries a LEDGER LINE, a ledger sticks out past the head on both sides, and it joins the column's horizontal-skylines like any other ink. The probe was measuring the unported ledger geometry (handoff section 2E) on top of the minimum. On g', which sits on a staff line and has no ledger, LilyPond saturates at 1.604200 -- exactly the rod probe N2N records -- for every width from 19.916929 down to 12.519213, and the dumped rods on every column read 1.604200 to the digit. The entry is read at 30mm (17.071654 ss), inside that plateau. SEEDED 2026-07-25. The note-to-note gap of a line squeezed until every spring sits on its MINIMUM -- the only regime in which a spring minimum is observable, and therefore the ledger key that removing GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 has to move. Ragged points read ideals at force 0; the justified pair reads a stretched line, whose inverse_stretch_strength LilyPond builds from the spacing INCREMENT and not from the skyline minimum (lily/spacing-basic.cc), which is why both of those opened exact and neither can see this. MEASURED: LilyPond's gap for this bar falls 3.048125 -> 2.037936 as the line narrows and then STOPS at 1.956300 for every width from 19.916929 down to 12.519213, so the entry is read at 30mm (17.071654 ss), inside the plateau. ⚠️ PREDICTION WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN AND WRONG: that it would saturate at the ROD, 1.604200, measured on probe N2N as the hard floor under the spring minimum 1.504200. It saturates 0.352100 above that, so the floor that actually binds a compressed line is NOT the rod N2N reads, and what sets it is not yet identified -- that is the open question this entry carries, and it must be answered before MinItemGap is touched, because a port aimed at 1.604200 would be aimed at the wrong number.

tab.staff.line-span.six-string.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION (-1.000000 -> 0). The DEFECT half of the tab string-spacing pair, against tab.staff.line-span.four-string as CONTROL. LilyPond's TabStaff sets StaffSymbol.staff-space = 1.5 for EVERY string count (ly/engraver-init.ly), so a six-string tab staff spans (6-1) * 1.5 = 7.500000 line centre to line centre; measured on 2.26.0 as staffY -7.600000..0.000000, the 7.6 being that 7.5 widened by half a line thickness at each edge (probe line-start-mindist.ly score CGT). Lily# instead TAPERS the spacing by string count -- EngravingDefaults.TabStringSpace returns 1.5 below five strings, 1.4 at five and 1.3 at six -- so it spans 5 * 1.3 = 6.500000, a full staff space short. The stated reason for the taper is that a five- or six-string staff should not grow too tall, which is a Lily# aesthetic judgement and not a LilyPond quantity; it also works AGAINST Lily#'s own (ratified, HANDOFF section 3) larger fret digits, whose 1.7875 height already overlaps a 1.3 string gap and is what the white occluding background exists to hide. The control lands on 1.5 by accident -- Lily#'s taper happens to agree with LilyPond below five strings -- which is what isolates the taper rather than the tab staff as a whole. THE FIX: TabStringSpace returns 1.5 for every string count, LilyPond's one value; the parameter is kept and deliberately unused so each call site says the spacing does not depend on it. MEASURED after: Lily# 7.500000000, residual 0.000000000 EXACT, with the four-string control unmoved at 0 -- the fix moved the taper and nothing else. Impact: five- and six-string tab staves grow (a six-string staff 6.5 -> 7.5 tall), which also gives the deliberately larger fret digits more room; every five- or six-string tab snapshot re-bases.

tab.staff.line-span.four-string.why: The CONTROL half of the tab string-spacing pair. A four-string tab staff spans (4-1) * 1.5 = 4.500000 on both sides -- LilyPond by its one staff-space of 1.5, Lily# because EngravingDefaults.TabStringSpace's taper happens to return 1.5 below five strings. It is exact from the moment it was opened, which is the point: a control that is already exact while the six-string half is 1.000000 short proves the defect is the TAPER and not the tab staff's geometry generally. Measured on 2.26.0: space=1.500000 lines=4 staffY=-5.192000..-0.592000, a 4.6 extent over the 4.5 span (probe line-start-mindist.ly score CG4). ⚠️ Keep this pinned when the taper goes: it must stay exact while the six-string half closes, or the fix moved the wrong thing.

line-start.clef-to-time.tab.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION (+0.235 -> 0), paired with line-start.clef-to-time.treble as the CONTROL. Same quantity, same measurement, one difference: a TabStaff under the notation staff. LilyPond's TAB clef is an ordinary Clef grob (ly/engraver-init.ly TabStaff clefGlyph = "clefs.tab") and is WIDER than the G clef -- origin-to-ink-right 2.8 against 2.565 -- so it widens the shared Clef break-align group and pushes the meter column (Clef.space-alist time-signature extra-space 1.52) right with it. Rendered on 2.26.0: notation CLEF anchor 0.800 (ink 0.800..3.365), TABCLEF anchor 0.800 (ink 1.000..3.600), TIME anchor 5.120 => clef->time 4.320000, against the treble control's 4.085000. The 0.235000 between them IS the TAB clef's ink advantage; the pair's LilyPond side differs by exactly that, so a Lily# reading that made them EQUAL was the defect. OPENED at residual +0.235: SpacingRules.MaxClefWidth walked only NON-tab staves, so the tab staff contributed nothing to the group however wide its clef, and Lily# printed the control's 4.085 here too. THE FIX: the group extent (SpacingRules.ClefGroupExtent) folds every staff that engraves a clef INCLUDING tab, taking clefs.tab's LILC bbox (0.2 . 2.8) -- newly generated, since the tab clef had never been in the metrics table -- and the renderer draws clefs.tab UNSCALED at that same group anchor, so the width booked is the width drawn. Before the fix Lily# scaled the glyph to the staff height (tabHeight/5.78) and drew it at systemStartX with no LeftEdge->clef 0.8 at all, which is why it could not be booked. Verified against the tab staff LilyPond actually draws (probe line-start-mindist.ly, scores CGT and CG4: staff-space 1.5, clef 5.760000 tall unscaled and centred on the middle line, overhanging a 4-string staff). Impact: every tab score re-bases -- the TAB clef changes size and moves onto the clef column, and on notation+tab scores the meter and first note move 0.235 right.

line-start.clef-to-time.percussion.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (+0.565000 -> 0), the LAST remnant of defect-3 (the PERCUSSION clef). Unlike a pitched clef, whose ink starts at the grob origin (ext-left 0), the percussion glyph's ink begins 0.67 ss RIGHT of its origin. Rendered on 2.26.0 (barline-spacing.ly score DCP): CLEF anchor 0.13, ext (0.67 . 2.0) => ink-left 0.8 (the LeftEdge->clef offset every clef shares), ink-right 2.13; the meter binds 1.52 off that ink right edge => TIME at 3.65, so the clef-anchor -> time-anchor distance is 3.65 - 0.13 = 3.520000. OPENED at residual +0.565000 (predicted to the digit before measuring): Lily# reserved GClefWidth (2.565) for the percussion clef via LineStartClefWidth's fallback AND drew the glyph at its origin (x + ClefGlyphXOffset) without the 0.67 ink-left offset, so its clef anchor sat at 0.8 (not 0.13) and its time flowed to 0.8 + 2.565 + 1.52 = 4.885 => the twin read 4.085 (the treble value), residual 4.085 - 3.52 = +0.565 -- EQUAL to the treble twin, the cross-check that both the width AND the origin were the fixed-treble approximation. THE FIX (two threaded quantities): (1) GlyphMetricsGenerated now carries ClefPercussion (LILC bbox 0.67,-1.0,2.0,1.0, extracted from the font like every other clef) and GlyphMetrics.LineStartClefWidth returns its ink WIDTH ClefPercussion.Right - Left = 1.33 (not the 2.565 fallback), so the shared clef column and the meter it break-aligns reserve the real width; (2) GlyphMetrics.ClefInkLeft returns ClefPercussion.Left 0.67 and SharedRenderer.DrawClef draws the glyph at x + ClefGlyphXOffset - ClefInkLeft, shifting the percussion origin to 0.13 so its ink-left lands on the shared 0.8 column exactly as LilyPond places it. Both are no-ops for the pitched clefs (ink-left 0). MEASURED after: Lily# 3.520000000, residual -0.000000000 EXACT. Impact: the percussion line-start meter and metered first note move ~1.235 LEFT (the over-reserved 2.565 - 1.33) and the percussion clef GLYPH shifts 0.67 left onto its true ink column; snapshots with a percussion clef (drum-groove) re-base. This closes defect-3 for every clef family.

line-start.time-signature-cross-staff-al.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (was ~3.05, now 0). Cross-staff meter alignment in a grand staff whose staves carry DIFFERENT keys (upper transposed to D major = 2 sharps, lower concert C major = none). LilyPond break-aligns the TimeSignature into ONE column spanning both staves -- the KeySignature break-align GROUP extent is the union across staves (break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142, g->extent(g,X_AXIS) over the group; :242 offsets the next column from extents[idx][RIGHT], the union RIGHT), so both meters print PAST the WIDEST key, at the same x. RENDERED on 2.26.0 (barline-spacing.ly score TSA): both TIME grobs at x=7.6534 (CLEF 0.8, the shared KEY column 4.3034 even for the empty lower key, HEAD 11.3534) -- spread 0. This is a METRIC-FREE probe: it compares two glyph anchors in the SAME render, depending on no ink width, so LP's 0 is exact by alignment, not a measured distance. BEFORE the fix Lily# spaced each staff's meter off its OWN key, so the concert staff's meter sat ~3.05 LEFT of the transposed staff's (its fixture transpose-multistaff read upper 8.05 vs lower 5.0) -- the fixture comment even claimed 'Verified against LilyPond', falsified by rendering LP. THE FIX: SharedRenderer draws every staff's meter at the system-wide MAX of the per-staff meter x (sharedTimeX = the widest key's column), so a same-key score is byte-identical and only differing-per-staff-key scores re-align. MEASURED after: Lily# spread 0.000000, EXACT. The absolute meter x also now matches LP (see line-start.clef-to-time.keyed): the KeySigTrailingGap 0.4 that DrawKeySignature once added to the drawn column, but the break-align reservation omitted, was removed so draw and reserve are one key-ink-measured model.

line-start.clef-to-time.keyed.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION (+0.4 -> 0). Clef -> time on a KEYED staff (D major, 2 sharps): the meter binds through the KEY, not the clef -- KeySignature.space-alist (time-signature . (extra-space . 1.15)) off the key's ink RIGHT edge, no pad. Rendered on 2.26.0: CLEF 0.8, KEY 4.185 (ext 2.2), TIME 7.535 => clef->time 6.735. The Lily# meter drew a KeySigTrailingGap 0.4 further right than the layout reserved -- a draw-vs-reserve split (SS 5.2.1(2)): DrawKeySignature returned key-ink + 0.4 for the meter to flow from, while BreakAlignSpacing reserved the note column off key-ink alone. THE FIX: the drawn time column (SharedRenderer.sharedTimeX) now uses KeySignatureInkWidth (the ink alone, = the reservation), and DrawKeySignature's now-dead +0.4 return was dropped. MEASURED after: Lily# 6.735000000, residual 0.000000000 EXACT -- confirming Lily#'s key ink width already matches LP's 2.2, so the 0.4 pad was the whole of the split. Impact: every keyed score's drawn line-start meter moves 0.4 LEFT onto the reserved column (first notes, layout-driven, do not move); snapshots with a key + time signature re-base.

line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-k.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-0.095264567 -> 0 exact). The CONTROL of the KCS/KCC custom-key pair was non-zero the moment it opened -- the keyed+metered line-start time->first-note regime had no point. LilyPond: head at the meter's ink RIGHT + 2.0 (TimeSignature.space-alist (first-note . (semi-shrink-space . 2.0)), natural length under ragged-right): TIME 7.535, ink 1.700000, HEAD 11.235 => 3.700000. The residual went through TWO wrong decompositions before the PNG showed the truth: (1) 'gap 1.9 vs 2.0' -- refuted by reading FirstNoteSpring, whose time arm is (2.0, 1.0) = LP exactly; (2) 'grob ext vs Pango advance of the digits' -- refuted by LOOKING at the render: Lily# (like LilyPond) draws the default 4/4 as the common-time C GLYPH, not digits. LilyPond's default style prints ONLY 2/2 and 4/4 as glyphs (timesig.C22/C44 -- scm/time-signature-settings.scm:954-964,981-982 make-c-time-signature-markup) and every other fraction as \number markup; the C44 LILC ink is 1.700000 (extracted from the font, = the measured grob ext to the digit). Lily# drew the C glyph but reserved the DIGIT path's Pango width 1.604735433. THE FIX: GetTimeSigWidth mirrors LP's style branch -- (4,4)->TimeSigCommon.Width, (2,2)->TimeSigCutCommon.Width (both LILC 1.7, newly extracted), else the Pango digit path unchanged (barline.next.time-change-to-notehead stays exact on it); DrawTimeSignature's invented flat 2.0 return replaced by the same widths. Every 4/4 first system's notes move +0.095264567 right (snapshot re-base, justified by this key and cut-common going exact).

system.knee-beam-notes.why: EXACT, and what it settles is that a KNEE is a structural divergence that does not reach the page. LilyPond leaves only CROSS-staff grobs out of the vertical skylines (lily/axis-group-interface.cc:850-858, its own comment), so a same-staff kneed Beam and its Stems ARE in them; Lily# seeds NEITHER — SkylineBuilder.AddBeamsToSkyline skips IsKnee and BeamedItemsToSuppress skips it too, so each member keeps the per-note FIXED 3.5 stem, in the member's OWN direction (AddNoteBoxToSkylines takes note.StemUp). WHY THAT SUBSTITUTE IS ENOUGH HERE: a knee's stems point INWARD — the low note stems up to the beam, the high note down to it — so the band and both stems live BETWEEN the two heads, and the heads are the envelope either way. LilyPond's own numbers say the same: its kneed ink TOP is 8.545000 above the refpoint, exactly d''''`s head (8.0 + 0.545), with no beam above it. THE POINT IS NOT SITTING ON A FLOOR, which is what makes it worth keeping: 18.090000 is neither the 12.000000 system-system basic-distance nor the 20.285000 the SAME music gives with the knee forbidden (\override Beam.auto-knee-gap = #100, probe book KNEC) — so the knee is worth 2.195000 of vertical room and this entry is measuring the kneed envelope itself. A future port that seeds the knee's band with the wrong geometry moves this number. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN and held: exact. ⚠️ TWO FIXTURE ERRORS ARE RECORDED IN THE PROBE HEADER, both the same trap: the first control was the same shape WITHOUT the leap (so its 6.090000 was almost all d''''`s own ink, not the knee), and the first pair had 4 bars with an explicit break where Lily# fitted all four on ONE system and the gap could not be read at all.

line-start.clef-to-time.mixed-key-grand-.why: EXACT, and it is a CONTROL for a defect that lives one layer away — raised so the fix for that defect cannot be applied in the wrong direction. WHAT IS MEASURED: clef to meter on a grand staff where only the UPPER staff engraves a signature (its part is transposed, so it prints D major = 2 sharps, beside a concert-pitch C-major lower staff). The distance therefore SPANS a key column that the score-level key knows nothing about — the score key here is C major, which books nothing at all. LilyPond dumps CLEF 0.800000, KEY 4.303400 (ext 2.200000), TIME 7.653400, first HEAD 11.353400; Lily# reproduces 6.853400 to 9 digits, because its line-start reservation unions the staves' OWN signatures (SpacingRules.WidestActiveKeyInk / ActiveKeyInkForStaff, the model built for line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-keyed). ⚠️ THE SIBLING POINT CANNOT SEE THIS: line-start.time-signature-cross-staff-alignment is an identity (both meters at one x) and holds however wide the shared key column is, INCLUDING not at all. THE DEFECT THIS GUARDS AGAINST: the BREAK GATE prices the same line start from score.LeadingKey instead (SystemBreaker.cs:66-69, IncrementalCompiler.cs:170-174), which on this score books 6.703400 against the layout's 9.353400 — 2.650000 short, being the key's 2.200000 plus the Clef->Key and Key->Time gaps that only open when a signature is engraved. That is a Lily#-internal disagreement with no LilyPond number of its own (LilyPond's breaker uses the real spacing — constrained-breaking.cc — so it HAS no second model), and it is held by SpacingInvariantTests.BreakGateAndLayout_PriceTheSameLineStart rather than by a corpus point: its only visible consequence is a line break, and a break flips inside a 2.650000 window, which would make a knife-edge ledger entry. When that gate is fixed, the fix must move the GATE up to this number and not this number down to the gate — which is what this point exists to say.

line-start.time-to-first-note.custom-key.why: CLOSED IN TWO STEPS THE SAME SESSION (-2.745264567 -> -0.095264567 -> 0 exact; the second step is the shared C-glyph meter width, see line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-key).The defect: the same two sharps declared as a CUSTOM signature reserved NO key column, because the reservation read KeySignature.Sharps only (WidestActiveKeySharps and the KeySignatureChangeItem scan dropped Custom; a custom key is KeySignature(0, custom), MeasureCollector.Form.cs:385) while the draw walk drew the signature -- the drawn meter overlapped the first note. THE FIX: one key-width model. SpacingRules.KeySignatureInkWidth(KeySignature) is now the single source (custom = per-glyph advance sum, standard = count x advance); SolvePrefixColumns/CalculatePrefixWidth/FirstNoteSpring take the key INK width instead of a sharps count; WidestActiveKey returns the full KeySignature record, widest by ink (the break-align group extent is an ink union, break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142), and preserves Custom through mid-piece key changes; MultiStaffScore.LeadingKey replaces LeadingKeySharps. LilyPond's KCC dump is byte-identical to KCS (one key model, keyAlterations) and Lily# now mirrors that structure. The whole existing corpus is byte-invariant (standard keys compute the identical width; zero snapshots moved).

line-start.time-to-first-note.cut-common.why: OPENED EXACT as the cut-common half of the C-glyph width pair (with line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-key). LilyPond's default style prints ONLY 2/2 and 4/4 as glyphs (timesig.C22/C44, make-c-time-signature-markup); C22's LILC ink is 1.700000 like C44's, so time -> first note is 3.700000 for BOTH -- the pair's equality is the cross-check that the two C widths ride one (glyph) path while every other fraction stays on the Pango digit path. Lily# reserved 2/2 from the digit table too (GetTimeSigWidth max digit '2' = 1.4657 Pango) under a drawn cut-C glyph; the same fix (GetTimeSigWidth's LP-style branch) closes both.

line-start.ossia-key-alignment.sharps.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-3.365 -> 0 exact). The ossia (no clef on its first appearance) above a keyed main staff: its key signature must sit in the ONE KeySignature break-align column spanning the system, exactly like the grand-staff clef/time columns (break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142, group extent = union across staves). METRIC-FREE: ossia key X minus main key X in the same render; LilyPond prints 0 (OKEY anchor == KEY anchor == 4.185, for the NR fontSize+staff-space recipe AND under \magnifyStaff -- probe scores OKN/OKM). The PREDICTION written before the LP dump said 'LeftEdge -> key-signature extra-space 0.8 (define-grobs.scm:2097)' -- the dump REFUTED it: column sharing wins; the 0.8 alist entry never binds because the system-wide Clef column exists (the main staff has a clef). Lily# drew the ossia key at systemStartX + Clef->Key 0.82 off a clef that was not there. THE FIX: the drawn walk places every staff's key at the SHARED key column (sharedKeyX = widest-clef right + Clef->Key), the same expression the reservation's SolvePrefixColumns KeyX carries -- for a staff with a clef this is byte-identical to the former per-staff walk, so only the ossia moved. ALSO fixed with it, per the coordinate-frame rule: the ossia signature's INTERNAL glyph advances were unscaled (1.1 real ss inside a magstep(-3) staff -- mixed frames); DrawKeySignature now scales its advances by the staff's notation scale, matching LP's scaled stencil (OKN dump: OKEY ink 1.5558 ~ 2.2 x magstep(-3); the sub-0.1% remainder is LP's design-size font metrics, the clef-sliver family, not opened here).

line-start.ossia-key-alignment.flats.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-3.365 -> 0 exact). Flats half of the ossia key-alignment pair (B-flat major; see the sharps entry for the mechanism and the fix). LilyPond: OKEY == KEY == 4.185, offset 0 -- the same 0 as sharps, the pair's content-independence cross-check. Lily# now prints 0 on both halves: the shared key column is one expression, so it cannot depend on the key's content.

line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-concer.why: CLOSED TO EXACT (+0.400000 -> 0) by porting merge_springs. CONTROL of the tab-key pair (a tab staff beside a concert notation staff, both in C major). It opened NON-ZERO and its residual was NOT the defect the pair was cut for: the LilyPond value is 3.300000, not the single-staff 3.700000 of KCS/KC2, because the line-start spring is merge_springs (spring.cc:104) AVERAGING one wish per staff and the two staves wish for different things -- their last prefatory grob differs. Notation staff: last grob TimeSignature, (first-note . (semi-shrink-space . 2.0)), staff-spacing.cc:193-198 -> fixed 6.82+1.0, ideal 8.82. Tab staff: last grob Clef, (first-note . (minimum-fixed-space . 5.0)), :183-187 -> ink-left 1.0 + max(2.6, 5.0) = 6.0, then the SHARED min_dist floor (:212-215, 0.3 + min_dist) lifts it to 8.02. Average (8.82+8.02)/2 = 8.42 = TIME ink right 6.82 + 1.6. Two ORDINARY staves keep 3.700000 exactly (measured on a treble+bass twin: TIME 5.0034 -> HEAD 8.7034) because equal wishes average to themselves -- which is why no earlier multi-staff point could see this. THE FIX, ported literally: spacing-spanner.cc:492-517 breakable_column_spacing collects one Staff_spacing wish per staff from the left column's spacing-wishes and ends in merge_springs, so LineStartColumn.LineStartSpring now builds one wish per staff (LineStartColumn.PrefatoryGrobs -> Spacing_interface::extremal_break_aligned_grob, spacing-interface.cc:190-230, which SKIPS empty extents -- that is why a tab staff's stencil-less TimeSignature drops out and its TAB clef becomes the extremal grob) and Spring.MergeSprings averages them (spring.cc:101-129, N at once). The prediction written before the measurement -- both halves exact, no other ledger point moving -- held for this half to 15 digits and for every other point; the keyed half kept a small residual from a SECOND defect, recorded there.

line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-keyed.why: CLOSED TO EXACT IN THREE STEPS (+7.450000 -> +0.400000 -> +0.067135965 -> 0), and the LAST step was a defect this pair EXPOSED rather than one it was cut for. After merge_springs went in, the control half (tab-concert) was exact while this half kept +0.067135965 -- and the pair's LilyPond side is an IDENTITY (TKC and TKT dump equal to 15 digits, because nothing engraves the tab part's key), so any difference between the two Lily# halves is a Lily# defect by construction. It was this: Lily# attached an ACCIDENTAL to a tab staff's notes. LilyPond removes the Accidental_engraver from both TabVoice and TabStaff (ly/engraver-init.ly:1189, :1213, 'No accidental in tablature !'), so a tab note has no Accidental grob at all -- it neither draws NOR reserves. Lily# spelled the tab part's `c,` in F# major as c-natural (accidentals are decided once per PART, before the score binds it to a staff) and let that phantom natural into the spacing: MusicalColumnLeftReach 0.100000 -> 1.234272 on every tab note, i.e. 1.13 ss of blank paper in front of every fret number, which raised the measure's own spring-0 minimum by 0.134272; LineStartSpringForLine floors the tab staff's Staff_spacing wish at that minimum (the LILYSHARP-OWN grace/lyric floor) and merge_springs halved it: 0.134272 / 2 = 0.067136, to 15 digits. THE FIX is TabResolver.RemoveAccidentals, applied to the tab staff's own copy of the voice -- the same context boundary LilyPond removes the engraver at, so the same part on a notation staff beside it keeps its accidentals and a shared paper column still sees THOSE. Measured: min_dist was NOT what moved (7.720000 on both halves before and after); the tab clef's box never reached as far as the notation staff's meter. HISTORY OF THE EARLIER STEPS: the defect half is the SAME score as TKC with the tab part opening in F# major (6 sharps). Nothing engraves that key -- LilyPond's TabStaff removes the Key_engraver (engraver-init.ly:1214) and Lily# draws no key on a tab staff either -- so the two LilyPond twins are geometrically IDENTICAL (all 13 dumped grobs equal to 15 digits) and the pair's LP side is an identity. Lily# disagreed by exactly 7.050000000 = Clef->Key 0.82 + 6-sharp ink 6.6 + Key->Time 1.15 - Clef->Time 1.52, the prediction written before the measurement, to 15 digits: SpacingRules.WidestActiveKey walked EVERY staff (tab, text row and ossia included) while the drawn walk skipped tab/text/ossia, so the reservation booked a key column nobody engraves and shoved the first note that far right of the meter it is spaced from -- a gaping hole, with no fixture in the corpus to show it. THE FIX is the break-align group itself, ported literally: one predicate (SpacingRules.ContributesToKeyColumnWidth = the staves that ENGRAVE a signature, tab and text rows removing their Key_engraver per engraver-init.ly:1214,297) selects the staff set for BOTH the reservation and the drawn shared-time walk, and both union the ENGRAVED widths (WidestActiveKeyInk -> EngravedKeyInkWidth), which is what break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142 unions. An ossia is IN that union like any Staff, contributing its reduced-size stencil (probe OKN: ossia key ink 1.5558 = 2.2 * magstep(-3) at the unscaled shared column X) -- the reservation now carries a WIDTH rather than one staff's KeySignature, which is what makes a scaled contribution expressible at all. The pair read as an identity on the Lily# side too (both halves 3.700000), the cross-check that the staff set was the whole of what differed THEN; the residual left on both was the merge_springs averaging recorded under tab-concert, closed since.

staffless.line-start.chords-vs-staff.why: CLOSED (-0.438600 -> 0) BY PORTING THE ChordName ANCHOR, 2026-07-25, and it closed at the number the point had already named. WHAT IS MEASURED: the same progression over a staff minus the same progression alone, a difference of two anchors read the same way on each side -- so the point is blind to a symmetric convention error and stays blind now that the convention is right (LpGeometryLedgerTests.ChordSymbolsAreAnchoredAtTheirInkLeft is what asserts THAT). WHY IT WAS OPEN: Lily# centred a chord symbol on its column (TextAnchor.Middle) and LilyPond does not. CS was already right on both sides -- both engravers put the first symbol on 8.585000 -- so the whole disagreement was CO, the staff-LESS half: LilyPond stands its first column on 0.500000 (standard_breakable_column_spacing's min_dist + 0.5 with min_dist 0, spacing-basic.cc:71-77) and its ChordName sits ON that column with its ink starting there, because ChordName declares no X-offset and no self-alignment-interface at all (scm/define-grobs.scm:837-855). Lily# reached the same 0.500000 spring, then hung half the symbol left of the column, and the keep-inside-line rod (simple-spacer.cc:431-432,556-560) correctly refused to let that ink cross the margin: it pushed the column out to the half width 0.938600, and 0.938600 - 0.500000 = 0.438600 was this residual to 6 digits. THE FIX WAS THE ANCHOR ALONE -- the spring and the rod were already LilyPond's and neither was touched. The symbol is now drawn with TextAnchor.Start, its keep-inside-line reach is its WHOLE width to the right and nothing to the left, and its spacing reservation is the matching asymmetric (-0.5 . w + 0.5) of extra-spacing-width. The rod then goes inert on a staff-less line and the column falls back to the bare 0.500000. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN and held to 9 digits: 8.085000000. The user was asked first, because centring might have been a deliberate divergence like the tab fret size (docs/HANDOFF.md section 3); the decision was to follow LilyPond. ⚠️ Chord GRIDS are a DIFFERENT grob and are NOT covered by this: GridChordName centres its ink in the measure square (grid-chord-name::calc-X-offset, scm/output-lib.scm:3744-3768), and Lily#, having no measure squares, leaves its chords-only sheet on the ChordName path. As predicted, meter-identity, key-identity and chord-symbol-over-notehead did not move -- none of them can see a symmetric shift.

staffless.line-start.meter-identity.why: EXACT, and it guards a defect that was live until 2026-07-25. The pair's LilyPond side is an IDENTITY: a ChordNames context has no Time_signature_engraver (ly/engraver-init.ly:703-725), so the same chords under 3/4 and under 4/4 put their first symbol on 0.500000 both times, to 15 digits -- which makes any Lily# difference the size of a Lily# defect by construction. Lily# used to book GetTimeSigWidth(beats, beatType) into the line-start prefix of a system with no staff, and that width is NOT the same for 4/4 and 3/4, so this pair would have opened at the difference between the two meter stencils. SpacingRules.AnyStaffEngravesTime now asks whether any row engraves a meter before the prefix books one. ⚠️ EXACT here means 'the meter column is shut', not 'the line start is right': a symmetric error cancels out of an identity by definition, and one was live underneath this point until 2026-07-25 -- these same scores stood 0.438600 away from LilyPond in absolute terms the whole time it read 0, which is what chords-vs-staff was opened to say.

staffless.line-start.key-identity.why: EXACT. The second identity of the staff-less prefix: ChordNames has no Key_engraver either (ly/engraver-init.ly:703-725), so the same chords in E major and in C major are geometrically identical on LilyPond's side. This half was ALREADY closed before the point existed -- SpacingRules.ContributesToKeyColumnWidth excludes a text row, the fix made for line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-keyed -- so it opened exact, and that is the finding: it is a CONTROL proving the key column really is shut for a text row, and the reason the clef and meter columns could be fixed without disturbing it. Same caveat as meter-identity: an identity cannot see a symmetric error.

staffless.lead-sheet.narrow-syllable-flo.why: CLOSED (0.151200 -> 0) BY PORTING THE ALIGNMENT EXTENT, 2026-07-25, together with its three siblings. Lily# placed a syllable at -w/2 and LilyPond at -w/2 + he.centre, so Lily# reached past the line-start spring where LilyPond does not. WHAT IS MEASURED: adding a LYRIC row to a chords-only staff-less line must not move the first column at all, and on LilyPond's side it does not -- CLI and CO both stand it on 0.500000, so this pair's LilyPond half is an IDENTITY and any Lily# difference is a Lily# defect by construction, in Lily#'s own units, with no LilyPond text metric in it. THAT IS THE POINT OF THE NARROW SYLLABLE. LilyPond centres a syllable on the PaperColumn placeholder X-alignment-extent (0 . 1.35) -- self-alignment-interface.cc:117-176 with self-alignment-X = left-align-at-split-notes returning CENTER when the column holds no note heads (output-lib.scm:1642-1673), define-grobs.scm:2749-2750 -- giving x = -w/2 + 1.35/2. The keep-inside-line rod is a MINIMUM (simple-spacer.cc:556-560), so while w/2 - 0.675 stays under the 0.5 that standard_breakable_column_spacing already gives (spacing-basic.cc:71-77), the rod is SLACK and the column never moves. MEASURED: CLI's syllable is 0.990156 wide and sits 0.179922 to the RIGHT of its column (-0.495078 + 0.675 = 0.179922, exact); CLA's is 1.365732 and reaches 0.007866 left, a real reach that still does not bind; both columns dump 0.500000. Lily# has no placeholder: its reach is w/2, which clears 0.5 for any syllable over 1.0 ss, so the rod binds and the column leaves the floor. Lily#'s "I" is 1.302400 in its own serif at 3.2 ss, and 1.302400/2 - 0.500000 = 0.151200 = this residual to 9 digits. THE FIX is the placeholder in the lyric's offset; the rod and the spring are already LilyPond's. A raw comparison on the WIDE-syllable CL cannot do this job: the two engravers do not measure the same w (Lily#'s lyric face is ~27% wider -- "Twin" 7.587200 against LilyPond's 5.975079), so a CL point would mix the missing 0.675 with a font metric. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN, both sides: LilyPond 0.000000 and Lily# +0.151200; both held. ⚠️ IT IS STILL WORTH KEEPING NOW THAT IT IS EXACT, and not because it re-states the sibling points: it is the only one that watches the SPACING side, i.e. that the keep-inside-line rod is fed the syllable's reach FROM ITS ALIGNMENT POINT rather than from its column. A port that fixed the drawn offset and left the rod input centred would draw the syllable correctly and still shove the column.

staffless.lead-sheet.narrow-syllable-wid.why: CLOSED (0.238400 -> 0) with its siblings, 2026-07-25. It said something the floor point did not: inside that floor window LilyPond's first column is BLIND to the syllable's width, and Lily#'s tracks it. The two scores differ in one letter -- "I" against "a" -- and nothing else, so LilyPond's half is again an IDENTITY (both columns 0.500000, even though the syllables are 0.990156 and 1.365732 wide and the wider one does reach 0.007866 left of its column). Lily# moves by exactly half the width difference: (1.779200 - 1.302400)/2 = 0.238400, this residual to 9 digits, which is the signature of a grob CENTRED on its column with the rod passing that half width straight through. ⚠️ THIS IS KEPT SEPARATE FROM narrow-syllable-floor ON PURPOSE. That one could be closed by any constant that happens to push Lily# back onto the floor for this one syllable; this one cannot -- it fails for as long as the column responds to w at all in the regime where LilyPond's does not. Porting x = -w/2 + 0.675 closed both, because w/2 - 0.675 is negative for both syllables and Lily# now lands on the same 0.5 floor. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN: LilyPond 0.000000, Lily# +0.238400; both held, and the port took both to 0 as predicted.

lyric.syllable-centre.placeholder-column.why: CLOSED (-0.675000 -> 0) ON THE DAY IT WAS RAISED: Lily# centred a syllable ON its column where LilyPond centres it on the column's ALIGNMENT EXTENT, which is not the same point. WHAT IS MEASURED: the syllable's ink CENTRE minus its column, the one lyric quantity comparable across two engravers whose lyric faces differ -- with self-alignment-X and parent-alignment-X both CENTER, self-alignment-interface.cc:117-176 gives x = -w/2 + he.centre, so ink centre = column + x + w/2 = column + he.centre and the syllable's own width cancels identically. The column is read through the chord symbol standing on it, which IS the column (ChordName has no X-offset, scm/define-grobs.scm:837-855). LilyPond's answer here is 0.675000 = 1.35/2: a staff-less column holds no note heads, so Paper_column::get_interface_extent returns an EMPTY note-column extent and `he` falls back to the placeholder X-alignment-extent (0 . 1.35), 'as wide as a note head' (define-grobs.scm:2749-2750, self-alignment-interface.cc:121-139 -- LilyPond's own comment names lyrics without associatedVoice as the case). MEASURED and font-free by construction: probe scores CLI and CLA put the ink centre on 1.175000 over a column at 0.500000 for syllables of 0.990156 and 1.365732, i.e. 0.675000 both times. Lily# reported 0.000000 -- it drew the syllable centred on the column itself -- so the residual was the whole of he.centre, and it now reports 0.675000000. ⚠️ This is the DRAWN half of the defect; staffless.lead-sheet.narrow-syllable-floor and -width-blind are the SPACING half (the same missing offset seen through the keep-inside-line rod), and all four closed in one commit. THE PORT IS LilyPond's FORMULA, not this number: LyricEngraver adds he.centre from SpacingRules.ParentAlignmentCentresPerColumn, which unions the column's note heads and rests and falls back to EngravingDefaults.PaperColumnXAlignmentExtentWidth / 2 -- so 0.675 appears in the code exactly once, as half a grob property, and the staff-ful case reads a note head instead without a second constant.

lyric.syllable-centre.note-column.why: CLOSED (-0.688700 -> 0) with its siblings: the SAME defect on the branch that is normally taken. When the parent column holds note heads, `he` is their combined extent and the placeholder never comes into it (self-alignment-interface.cc:121-141), so LilyPond centres the syllable on the NOTE HEAD's centre rather than on a nominal 1.35. MEASURED (probe LSH, a plain vocal line): the head is 1.377400 wide and the syllable's ink centre sits 0.688700 right of its column -- half a note head, and NOT the 0.675000 the staff-less scores give. That the two numbers differ is what proves this branch is live rather than dead code for lyrics; the prediction written before the run named 'half a note head, not 0.675' with '0.675 again' as its falsifier, and the falsifier did not fire. Lily# reported 0.000000 here too: it centred on the column in both regimes, so it was not that Lily# ported one branch and missed the other -- it never had the offset at all. It now reports 0.688700000, reading the head's own box rather than a second constant. ⚠️ THIS POINT IS WHY THE PORT WRITES BOTH BRANCHES (section 5.2 'write every branch'). A port that only added 0.675 where there are no note heads would have closed the staff-less points and left every vocal score 0.688700 out, with nothing in the corpus to say so -- and 0.675 would have been WRONG here by 0.013700, which is small enough to look like rounding and never be questioned. ⚠️ WHAT IS IN `he` WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: probe LSA adds an accidental and LSD a dot, and BOTH leave this at 0.688700 (so neither joins the extent), while LSR replaces the head with a rest and gives 0.750000 (so a rest does). Two of those three predictions were written down first and were wrong; the port unions heads and rests only because of them.

staffless.chord-symbol-over-notehead.why: EXACT ON ARRIVAL, and the honest reading is that it measures LESS than it looks like it does. LilyPond's value is 0 by construction: over a staff its ChordName and the note head it stands over share an anchor exactly (score CS dumps both at 8.585000), because ChordName has no X-offset and no self-alignment-interface (scm/define-grobs.scm:837-855). Lily# agrees to 0.000000 -- the symbol IS on the note's column. ⚠️ What this CANNOT see is the anchor convention, and it did not see it when the convention was WRONG either: the recorder stores the ANCHOR POINT a text was drawn at, which is the column whether the ink is centred on it (Lily# until 2026-07-25) or starts at it (LilyPond, and Lily# since). This number was 0.000000 through both. It is kept as a cheap guard that a chord symbol stays bound to its note's column (a lead sheet where the symbol drifts off the note would show here), NOT as evidence the anchor convention is right -- LpGeometryLedgerTests.ChordSymbolsAreAnchoredAtTheirInkLeft asserts that directly, for exactly this reason.

page.natural.staff-staff-inside.why: EXACT. THE CONTROL of the pair that asks whether the distance between two staves of a system comes out of the PAGE's spring chain. Same music and same bar count as page.stretched.staff-staff-inside, on the same six-systems-per-page paper, with ragged-bottom on so nothing stretches. PREDICTION, written before running: 9.000000 on both sides -- staff-staff-spacing's basic-distance, because this music asks ensure_min_distance for less than that (the treble c hangs 3.545 below its middle line, the bass staff's deepest up-stem reaches 3.0 above its own, 3.545 + 3.0 + 1 = 7.545 < 9). Measured on LilyPond 2.26.0: 9.000000 on all three pages, and Lily# reads 9.000000 too, so the control is flat on both sides and every digit the stretched entry moves is the stretch. NOT SITTING ON A FLOOR in the sense HANDOFF 5.0 warns about: 9 is the spring's IDEAL, not its minimum, so a force reaches it -- which is exactly what the twin entry shows.

page.stretched.staff-staff-inside.why: THE STAFF SPRING INSIDE A SYSTEM, on a page that stretches. Page_layout_problem::append_system pushes one spring per spaceable staff into the SAME chain as the system-to-system springs (page-layout-problem.cc:651-720): ideal = staff-staff-spacing's basic-distance 9, inverse stretch strength = its stretchability 5 (define-grobs.scm:3352-3355). Lily# has no such spring -- PageLayouter.PositionSystemsOnPage builds one spring per SYSTEM boundary, and every system on every page is drawn at the score-wide MultiStaffLayouter.CalculateSystemHeight, the Align_interface minimum, at any force. PREDICTION, written before running: LilyPond 9 + 5f and Lily# 9.000000 flat, so the residual is the whole stretch. THE PREDICTION HELD AND ITS OWN FALSIFIER CONFIRMED IT: measured 9.495460 with the system gap on the same page at 17.945524, i.e. (9.495460 - 9) / 5 = 0.0990920 and (17.945524 - 12) / 60 = 0.0990921 -- one force, seven digits, which is only possible if the staff distance is a spring in that chain. Lily# reads 9.000000 -- the same number as the ragged control, on the same paper -- so the residual -0.495460 IS the stretch, in one piece, with nothing else mixed in. Read on PAGE 1; page 2 and the short page 3 solve to their own forces (both 9.491922 under the cap). This is also the answer to the older question of whether BuildSystemSkylines should offset the last staff by the MINIMUM translation (page-layout-problem.cc:1080-1095) or by the final position: today they are the same number in Lily# because nothing ever stretches them apart, so that divergence cannot be measured until this spring exists.

system.stretched-distance.two-staff.why: WHERE THE SLACK WENT INSTEAD. The SYSTEM spring on the same stretched page as page.stretched.staff-staff-inside, measured last-staff-refpoint to next-system-first-staff-refpoint (the probe script prints it from the raw doubles rather than leaving two F6 prints to be subtracted -- arithmetic on a rounded gap is how 3.544994 for 3.550000 got into system.stretched-distance). It is here because the slack has to go somewhere: LilyPond shares this page's stretch between 5 system springs at stretchability 60 and 6 staff springs at 5, while Lily# has only the system springs. PREDICTED DIRECTION, written before running: Lily#'s gap opens WIDER. IT DOES -- 18.319268 against 17.945524, i.e. Lily# solves the same page to force 0.105321 where LilyPond solves it to 0.099092. ⚠️ THE MAGNITUDE WAS NOT PREDICTED CORRECTLY and is NOT yet accounted for: the guess was +0.53 from sharing the same slack over 300 units of stretchability instead of 330, and the truth is +0.373744. The two chains differ in more than the staff springs (top-system-spacing, last-bottom-spacing and the ink extents that floor them are Lily#'s own numbers on this page: its first refpoint and foot slack are not LilyPond's either), so the arithmetic that would close this entry has not been done -- do not read the residual as 'the staff springs' share' until it has. What the entry IS good for: a port that adds the staff spring must close this and page.stretched.staff-staff-inside TOGETHER, and one that closes only the staff entry has moved the money rather than the model.

page.stretched.two-staff.staves-on-first.why: The structural guard for the three entries above, which read gaps by INDEX: gap 0 is a system's INSIDE distance and gap 1 the distance to the next system only while the page holds six two-staff systems. Six is forced on both sides (systems-per-page = 6 / PageBreakingParameters.SystemsPerPage), so this counts the staves that reached the page: 12.
